rationale: The extended probe now also reaches two-sided acknowledgement: polling for the majority side's own leader before writing lets both leaders commit and acknowledge a client write while partitioned, so the run shows a client write acknowledged on each side (both_sides_acknowledged true on the flagged case, false for the flag-off control where only the majority side acknowledges). FSM divergence and lost acknowledged entries are still not witnessed, because the applied-slice indexing did not line up with the conflict index and the heal window is short; that part is left open. This successor declares the two-sided acknowledgement as a bounded check for a receipt; the configuration, election and single-side acknowledgement comparisons remain as recorded.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs that keeps a stale, smaller configuration can acknowledge a client write while its support is a minority of the committed configuration: isolated together with one committed voter it became leader and its Apply completed, whereas the same restart without the flag produced no leader on that side and no acknowledgement.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the restarting node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, that partner also cut off from the majority side; two second apply timeout, bounded observation window, flag-off control in the same execution.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: Three completed comparisons, each with its flag-off control, answer this question. Configuration: receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 15 - the node restarted from a log whose latest configuration is index 14 with five servers came back at configuration index 1 with three servers - control holding at evaluated event index 18 (index 14, five servers). Election: receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 22 - isolated with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returned, the node became leader with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3, and the same run reports majority_side_leader true - control holding at evaluated event index 25. Client contract: receipt 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 27 - the isolated leader's Apply completed (minority_apply_ok true) while the flag-off control produced no leader there and no acknowledgement (comparison 1 holds, evaluated event index 29). Source: restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the startup scan at api.go:604-620, so AddVoter's later entry (api.go:994-1005) is never re-read and the node keeps the snapshot's three-server list; quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) then returns two, electSelf (raft.go:1999-2060) asks only that list, and the leader's commitment calculation (commitment.go:60-105) accepts the two matching indexes as a quorum, so the write is acknowledged against a majority of the stale configuration rather than of the committed one. The manoeuvre the runs needed - also cutting the single committed voter off from the majority side so requestVote's existing-leader guard (raft.go:1690-1700) does not refuse the vote - is an ordinary partition shape; the minority leadership reproduced in the two immediate-isolation executions and not in two settled-schedule executions, so the manifestation is schedule dependent while the decision and the acknowledgement are unrepaired by the library. A fourth check is under test: with a bounded wait for a majority-side leader before writing, a native run had both sides acknowledge a client write concurrently (both_sides_acknowledged true on the flagged case, false for the control, where only the majority side acknowledges), which the successor experiment re-runs for a receipt. Not witnessed: any FSM divergence or lost acknowledged entry, because the applied-slice comparison at the conflict index did not line up and no entry was recovered after healing.

7da03e78394f41fdad540ae0824ec2a6-gap-1.explanation: Election and acknowledgement are resolved by complete comparisons (abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 witness index 22 with control 25; 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db witness index 27 with control 29). Reproduction depends on whether the single committed voter on the isolated side still hears the majority-side leader, because requestVote refuses candidates while a leader is known (raft.go:1690-1700); with immediate isolation it reproduced in both executions, with the settled schedule it did not. Entry-level divergence still has no witness: no run produced a majority-side leader writing concurrently with the minority leader, so this part of the gap stays open.

counterevidence: The flag-off controls in all three receipts keep the committed configuration, cannot win on the isolated side and do not acknowledge a write there.

Two settled-schedule executions did not produce the minority leadership, and the difference is explained by whether the isolated partner still heard the majority-side leader; no frequency or absence claim is made.
The redundant configuration re-checks in one earlier receipt were incomplete because two scenarios emit the same restart event name; they carry no new claim and are not used.
limitations: No FSM divergence or lost acknowledged entry is witnessed: in the client-contract run the majority side had no leader, so only one side wrote.
Observed windows are bounded (five second election window, two second apply timeout, two second heal settle), so no occurrence-rate or absence bound is established.
The scenario restarts the former leader of an enlarged cluster with an added-voter change; other roles, change types and chain orders are not explored.
interpretations.joint_history: Three complete executions of the same five-voter scenario over identical stores, sizes and snapshot timing supply the three comparisons: b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 (configuration loss and its control, both reporting index 1 with three servers against expected 14 with five on the flagged side and 14 with five on the control), abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 (election and its control), and 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db (client acknowledgement and its control). Each receipt built its own cluster and stores and is a complete history in itself; only the comparison declarations and event names differ between them, and the configuration values agree across all three, so none is a fragment of another.

scope.description: Five-voter cluster whose leading node is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a snapshot predating the membership change, isolated with one committed voter immediately after the restart. Once the isolated node is leader and the majority side has its own leader, a client Apply is issued on both; the partition is healed, and the event reports whether both sides acknowledged. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: The isolated node's rebuilt configuration is the three-voter snapshot configuration, so two votes commit there while the committed configuration needs three.
A successful Apply is an acknowledgement to the client.
Waiting for both sides to hold leadership is a legal partition shape, not an injected fault.
excluded: FSM divergence and lost-entry claims; the applied-slice comparison at the conflict index did not line up and is not used.
Entry contents at the conflict index, which the probe reports as empty.

experiment.prefix: The harness reuses the multi-voter scenario construction (MakeClusterCustom with Peers 3, CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs; one deliberate Snapshot; MakeClusterNoBootstrap(2) merged with FullyConnect and two AddVoter calls; Shutdown and NewRaft on the same stores with a fresh inmem transport; Partition isolating the restarted node plus one committed voter with that pair reconnected). It waits for the isolated node to be leader, waits up to three seconds for a majority-side leader, applies a distinct command on each side, heals by reconnecting all transports, waits two seconds, and emits mvdiv_after_heal with both leaders' presence, both apply outcomes, the derived both_sides_acknowledged operand, the conflict index, the applied slice lengths and the FSM divergence flag; no production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns the acknowledgement it gives a client and the guarantee that a committed entry survives; with a stale rebuilt configuration both depend on a quorum of an obsolete membership.

comparisons.description: Two partitioned sides must not both acknowledge client writes while one of them holds only a minority of the committed configuration; the defect prediction is that both do.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side has no leader, so only the majority side acknowledges.

experiment.revision_reason: The probe now waits (bounded to three seconds) for the majority side to have its own leader before writing, so both sides can acknowledge concurrently, and the event carries a derived both_sides_acknowledged operand so the comparison is inspectable. Scenario, isolation, apply and heal steps are unchanged.
